title: Browser music player (library, search, shuffle, playlists)
prompt: Build a music player web app that runs in the browser. It is static: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules are fine) -- no npm, no build step, no backend. It must work when this folder is served by any static file server (e.g. `python -m http.server`) and opened at /index.html. The song library is already in music/: music/library.json lists 8 songs (id, title, artist, album, duration in seconds, and file, a path relative to the project root), and the audio files are next to it. Load the library from music/library.json at runtime (fetch it); don't copy it into the code, and don't edit or delete anything in music/. Organize the JavaScript by concern -- e.g. one module for the library, one for the player and its queue, one for shuffle, one for playlists and their storage, one for the UI -- not one big file. The page must expose these elements; the data-testid attributes are the contract. LIBRARY AND SEARCH: every song in the current view is an element with data-testid="song" and data-song-id="<id>" that shows its title and artist, in library.json order; clicking it plays that song. An <input data-testid="search"> filters the library view as you type to the songs whose title, artist or album contains the text (case-insensitive); clearing it shows every song again. An element with data-testid="show-library" switches the view back to the full library. PLAYBACK: exactly one <audio data-testid="audio"> element, which actually plays the song's file. data-testid="now-playing" shows the current song's title and artist. data-testid="play-pause" pauses and resumes; data-testid="next" and data-testid="prev" move through the current queue. The queue is the list the song was started from: the library view as shown at the time (all songs, or the search results) or a playlist. next on the last song goes to the first, prev on the first goes to the last, and when a song ends the next one starts by itself. SHUFFLE: data-testid="shuffle" toggles shuffle and carries aria-pressed="true" or "false". With shuffle on, the queue plays in a random order that keeps the current song first and plays every song of the queue exactly once before any repeats; turning shuffle on again makes a new random order. Turning shuffle off goes back to the queue's normal order, continuing from the current song. PLAYLISTS: an <input data-testid="playlist-name"> and a data-testid="create-playlist" button create a playlist with that name; an empty name, or a name that already exists, creates nothing. Each playlist is listed as data-testid="playlist" with data-playlist-name="<name>"; clicking it opens it, and the view then lists its songs in the order they were added as data-testid="playlist-song" elements with data-song-id; clicking one plays it with the playlist as the queue. Each song in the library view has a <select data-testid="add-to-playlist"> whose option values are the playlist names; choosing one adds that song to that playlist (a song already in it isn't added twice). In an open playlist each playlist-song has a data-testid="remove-from-playlist" button, and the open playlist has a data-testid="delete-playlist" button that deletes it. Playlists and their songs are saved in localStorage and are still there after the page is reloaded. TESTS AND DOCS: write unit tests for the logic that has no DOM in it (shuffle, queue order, playlists) that run with Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`, no npm packages), and a README.md that says how to serve and open the app and how to run the tests.

verify.description: Serves the project over HTTP and drives the real page in headless Chromium (Playwright): the library renders from music/library.json, search filters, songs actually play in the <audio> element, play/pause/next/prev and auto-advance follow the queue, shuffle plays every song once from the current one, playlists can be created, filled, played, edited and deleted and survive a reload; then `node --test` must pass. One PASS/FAIL line per check; exit 0 iff all pass.
